library(shiny)
library(plotly)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plots are drawn with plotly, so the browser renders them directly.
# This avoids Safari blocking R's canvas-based plots in Shinylive.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ui <- fluidPage(
  withMathJax(),
  titlePanel("Gaussian (Normal) Distribution — Interactive Learning Tool"),

  tabsetPanel(
    # --- Tab 1: Interactive App ---
    tabPanel("Interactive Application",
      sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
          numericInput("mu", "Mean (μ):", value = 0, step = 0.1),
          numericInput("sigma", "Standard Deviation (σ):", value = 1, min = 0.001, step = 0.1),
          radioButtons("mode", "Select Mode:",
                       choices = c("Use lower and upper bounds" = "bounds",
                                   "Use probability (central area)" = "prob"),
                       selected = "bounds"),

          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.mode == 'bounds'",
            numericInput("lower", "Lower Bound:", value = -1, step = 0.01),
            numericInput("upper", "Upper Bound:", value = 1, step = 0.01)
          ),

          conditionalPanel(
            condition = "input.mode == 'prob'",
            numericInput("p", "Central Probability (area between bounds):",
                         value = 0.68, min = 0.001, max = 0.999, step = 0.001)
          ),
          helpText("Mode 1: Enter lower & upper to get probability."),
          helpText("Mode 2: Enter probability to get bounds.")
        ),
        mainPanel(
          plotlyOutput("normPlot", height = "420px"),
          verbatimTextOutput("probOutput")
        )
      )
    ),

    # --- Tab 2: Explanation + Shape Characteristics ---
    tabPanel("About the Gaussian Distribution",
      fluidRow(
        column(10, offset = 1,
          h3("Overview"),
          p("The Gaussian (or Normal) distribution is a continuous probability distribution that describes how values of a variable are distributed symmetrically around the mean.
            It is characterized by its bell-shaped curve, where most values cluster near the mean, and probabilities taper off toward the tails."),

          h3("Formula"),
          p("$$f(x;\\mu,\\sigma) = \\frac{1}{\\sigma\\sqrt{2\\pi}} e^{-\\frac{(x-\\mu)^2}{2\\sigma^2}}$$"),

          h3("Key Characteristics"),
          tags$ul(
            tags$li("Symmetrical about the mean (mean = median = mode)."),
            tags$li("Fully defined by two parameters: mean (μ) and standard deviation (σ)."),
            tags$li("Approximately 68% of observations lie within ±1σ, 95% within ±2σ, and 99.7% within ±3σ (the 68–95–99.7 rule)."),
            tags$li("The total area under the curve equals 1."),
            tags$li("Asymptotic to the x-axis, extending from -∞ to +∞.")
          ),

          h3("Applications in Psychological and Educational Measurement"),
          tags$ul(
            tags$li("Modeling test score distributions."),
            tags$li("Standardizing scores (z, T, stanine, sten)."),
            tags$li("Defining confidence intervals and error bands."),
            tags$li("Interpreting percentile ranks and probabilities.")
          ),

          h3("Shape Characteristics: Skewness and Kurtosis"),
          p("While the Gaussian distribution is perfectly symmetrical (skewness = 0, kurtosis = 3),
             real-world data often deviate from this ideal shape.
             The following examples illustrate typical forms of skewness and kurtosis observed in empirical data.
             In the kurtosis panels the dashed curve is a normal distribution with the same variance, for comparison."),

          fluidRow(
            column(6, wellPanel(
              h4("Right (Positive) Skew"),
              plotlyOutput("rightSkewPlot", height = "220px"),
              p("Tail extends toward higher values (right side).
                 $$\\text{Mean} > \\text{Median} > \\text{Mode}$$")
            )),
            column(6, wellPanel(
              h4("Left (Negative) Skew"),
              plotlyOutput("leftSkewPlot", height = "220px"),
              p("Tail extends toward lower values (left side).
                 $$\\text{Mean} < \\text{Median} < \\text{Mode}$$")
            ))
          ),

          fluidRow(
            column(6, wellPanel(
              h4("Leptokurtic"),
              plotlyOutput("leptoPlot", height = "220px"),
              p("Sharper peak and heavier tails than the normal distribution
                 $$\\text{(Kurtosis} > 3)$$")
            )),
            column(6, wellPanel(
              h4("Platykurtic"),
              plotlyOutput("platyPlot", height = "220px"),
              p("Flatter peak and lighter tails than the normal distribution
                 $$\\text{(Kurtosis} < 3)$$")
            ))
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # When μ or σ changes, reset the bounds to μ ± σ
  observeEvent(list(input$mu, input$sigma), {
    req(is.numeric(input$mu), is.numeric(input$sigma), input$sigma > 0)
    updateNumericInput(session, "lower", value = input$mu - input$sigma)
    updateNumericInput(session, "upper", value = input$mu + input$sigma)
  })

  # One place that computes the bounds and the area for both modes
  bounds <- reactive({
    mu <- input$mu; sigma <- input$sigma
    req(!is.na(mu), !is.na(sigma), sigma > 0)

    if (input$mode == "bounds") {
      req(!is.na(input$lower), !is.na(input$upper))
      lower <- min(input$lower, input$upper)
      upper <- max(input$lower, input$upper)
      area  <- pnorm(upper, mu, sigma) - pnorm(lower, mu, sigma)
    } else {
      p <- input$p
      req(!is.na(p), p > 0, p < 1)
      tail  <- (1 - p) / 2
      lower <- mu + qnorm(tail) * sigma
      upper <- mu + qnorm(1 - tail) * sigma
      area  <- p
    }
    list(mu = mu, sigma = sigma, lower = lower, upper = upper, area = area)
  })

  # In probability mode, show the computed bounds in the bound boxes
  observeEvent(list(input$p, input$mode), {
    req(input$mode == "prob")
    b <- bounds()
    updateNumericInput(session, "lower", value = round(b$lower, 3))
    updateNumericInput(session, "upper", value = round(b$upper, 3))
  })

  output$normPlot <- renderPlotly({
    b <- bounds()
    mu <- b$mu; sigma <- b$sigma

    xs <- seq(mu - 4 * sigma, mu + 4 * sigma, length.out = 800)
    ys <- dnorm(xs, mu, sigma)
    top <- max(ys) * 1.05

    # Vertical reference lines: mean (solid) and μ ± kσ (dotted)
    vline <- function(x, dash, color, width) {
      list(type = "line", x0 = x, x1 = x, y0 = 0, y1 = top, xref = "x", yref = "y",
           line = list(dash = dash, color = color, width = width))
    }
    shapes <- c(list(vline(mu, "solid", "black", 2)),
                lapply(mu + c(-4:-1, 1:4) * sigma, vline, "dot", "#BBBBBB", 1))

    p <- plot_ly() |>
      add_lines(x = xs, y = ys, line = list(color = "blue", width = 2.5),
                name = "Density", hoverinfo = "x+y")

    lo <- max(b$lower, min(xs)); hi <- min(b$upper, max(xs))
    if (hi > lo) {
      xs_sh <- seq(lo, hi, length.out = 400)
      p <- p |>
        add_lines(x = xs_sh, y = dnorm(xs_sh, mu, sigma), fill = "tozeroy",
                  fillcolor = "rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.3)", line = list(width = 0),
                  name = sprintf("Area = %.4f", b$area), hoverinfo = "skip")
    }

    ticks <- mu + (-4:4) * sigma
    p |>
      layout(
        title  = list(text = sprintf("Normal Distribution: N(%.2f, %.2f²)", mu, sigma)),
        xaxis  = list(title = "Score (x)", tickvals = ticks,
                      ticktext = as.character(round(ticks, 2)), zeroline = FALSE),
        yaxis  = list(title = "Density", range = c(0, top), zeroline = FALSE),
        shapes = shapes,
        showlegend = FALSE
      ) |>
      config(displaylogo = FALSE)
  })

  output$probOutput <- renderPrint({
    b <- bounds()
    cat(sprintf("Mean (μ) = %.3f, SD (σ) = %.3f\n", b$mu, b$sigma))
    cat(sprintf("Lower = %.3f (z = %.2f)\nUpper = %.3f (z = %.2f)\n",
                b$lower, (b$lower - b$mu) / b$sigma,
                b$upper, (b$upper - b$mu) / b$sigma))
    cat(sprintf("Area between bounds (Probability) = %.4f\n", b$area))
  })

  # --- Skewness and kurtosis example plots ---
  shape_plot <- function(x, y, col, fill, ref = NULL) {
    p <- plot_ly() |>
      add_lines(x = x, y = y, fill = "tozeroy", fillcolor = fill,
                line = list(color = col, width = 2), hoverinfo = "skip")
    if (!is.null(ref)) {
      p <- p |> add_lines(x = x, y = ref, line = list(color = "#555555", width = 1.5, dash = "dash"),
                          hoverinfo = "skip")
    }
    p |>
      layout(xaxis = list(visible = FALSE), yaxis = list(visible = FALSE),
             showlegend = FALSE, margin = list(l = 5, r = 5, t = 5, b = 5)) |>
      config(displayModeBar = FALSE, staticPlot = TRUE)
  }

  output$rightSkewPlot <- renderPlotly({
    x <- seq(0, 8, length.out = 400)
    shape_plot(x, dgamma(x, shape = 2, rate = 1), "darkorange", "rgba(255, 153, 0, 0.3)")
  })

  output$leftSkewPlot <- renderPlotly({
    x <- seq(-8, 0, length.out = 400)
    shape_plot(x, dgamma(-x, shape = 2, rate = 1), "darkred", "rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.3)")
  })

  # Leptokurtic: t with 5 df (kurtosis = 9), scaled to unit variance
  output$leptoPlot <- renderPlotly({
    x <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 400)
    df <- 5; s <- sqrt(df / (df - 2))
    shape_plot(x, dt(x * s, df) * s, "blue", "rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.3)", ref = dnorm(x))
  })

  # Platykurtic: flat-topped generalized normal (beta = 4, kurtosis ≈ 2.19), unit variance
  output$platyPlot <- renderPlotly({
    x <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 400)
    beta <- 4
    alpha <- sqrt(gamma(1 / beta) / gamma(3 / beta))
    y <- beta / (2 * alpha * gamma(1 / beta)) * exp(-(abs(x) / alpha)^beta)
    shape_plot(x, y, "#008B00", "rgba(0, 204, 0, 0.3)", ref = dnorm(x))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
